Your job is to make sure their work is real, correctly aimed, and faithful to the sources.\n\nSCOPE: you may read anything, file inbox issues, and correct roadmap rows and blueprint prose. Do NOT edit Lean proofs \u2014 the provers own those files and you share one git index with them. If you find a wrong Lean statement, file it as an issue at the site and DM the owning lane.\n\nWHAT TO CHECK, in rough priority order:\n\n1. IS THERE REAL PROGRESS? Measure, do not read reports. The metric that matters is producers vs consumers of an unproduced hypothesis: `rep` (RepresentableBy) has ~0 producers in AJC and 7 in AJCR against ~35 and ~96 consumers. A lane that adds consumers is not advancing the headline. Report these counts at HEAD vs the run's base commit, and name any lane whose net contribution is new consumers.\n\n2. IS THE MATHEMATICS FAITHFUL TO THE REFERENCES? references/ holds Kleiman, Hartshorne, FGA-explained, Milne, abelian-varieties and more. Check that roadmap and blueprint statements match the cited source \u2014 same hypotheses, not just the same conclusion. CONVENTIONS ARE THE TRAP: projective vs proper, ample vs very ample, integral vs irreducible vs reduced, k-rational vs closed point, relative vs absolute. A theorem imported under the wrong convention is a hallucination that typechecks nowhere and blocks everything downstream. A cited lemma is absent unless it is in the citing file's import closure \u2014 grep cannot see that difference, so #check it.\n\n3. IS THE CHOSEN PATH RELEVANT? The headline is Picard/Pic^0 representability. For each active row ask what discharging it buys the headline. Kleiman's clause (1) assumes PROJECTIVE while this project's binders are smooth/proper/geometrically-integral \u2014 pic-b proved `smooth proper curve is projective` (Adelic.isProjective_of_smoothProperGeometricallyIntegral, axiom-clean), so check who still needs rewiring to it.\n\n4. IS THE REQUIRED INFRASTRUCTURE OWNED? mathlib v4.31 lacks projective-morphism theory (no ample, no very ample, no Proj for morphisms). If a needed substrate has no lane, say so loudly in the inbox and propose it as a row.\n\n5. ARE THE LANES COMMITTING ENOUGH? Commits are the durable record; uncommitted work dies with the session. Note lanes going long stretches without one. Also flag sessions that failed: a report reading \"Reading additional input from stdin...\" is a harness stdin bug, not a lane with nothing to do.\n\n6. IS THE BOARD HONEST? Delete or correct rows that are unfaithful, vacuous, or superseded \u2014 but never a row another lane owns at HEAD, and every deletion lands with the truer row that replaces it. A `rejected` row with `priority: high` reads as urgent; fix those mismatches.\n\nYOUR PEERS are the prover lanes pic-a, pic-b, pic-e, pic-f. Announce what you are auditing before you start. Do not archive a standing protection to shorten a list. Read I-1482 first: it is the current lane roster and supersedes I-0838's.\n\nReport what you MEASURED, separated from what you inferred. All rights reserved.\n     3\tReleased under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.\n     4\tAuthors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors\n     5\t-/\n     6\timport AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DegreeZero\n     7\timport AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtMap\n     8\t\n     9\t/-!\n    10\t# The degree at field points and the degree-zero Picard functor (G-D6/G-D7, SB-7)\n    11\t\n    12\tFor the challenge curve `C` over `k`, an étale Picard class `λ : picEt C T` on an\n    13\tarbitrary test object restricts along any field point `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T` to a class\n    14\tof the affine étale Picard group of `Spec K`, which collapses through the affine\n    15\tcomparison `picEtAffineEquiv` to a plus class in `PicEtAff C K` — whose degree\n    16\t`PicEtAff.degAff` (SB-6) is an honest integer.\n    17\t\n    18\t* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt λ t` — **the degree of an étale Picard class at a field\n    19\t  point** (gap G-D6): the plus-class degree of the restriction of `λ` along `t`.\n    20\t* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_picEtMap` / `degAt_picEtFunctor_map` — functoriality: the\n    21\t  degree of a restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at\n    22\t  the composed field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting, which is what makes the\n    23\t  degree-zero subfunctor stability definitional.\n    24\t* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Subgroup C T` — the subgroup of classes of degree zero at\n    25\t  *every* field point of `T` (membership: `mem_pic0Subgroup_iff`).\n    26\t* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Functor C : (Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat` — **the\n    27\t  degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup\n    28\t  subfunctor of `picEtFunctor C` cut out by the degree-zero condition, the binding\n    29\t  carrier of the Wave-4 representability statement (`RepresentableBy`, design §2.7).\n    30\t  The restriction maps are `pic0Map`, with underlying-class equation `pic0Map_coe`\n    31\t  (the naturality square of the inclusion, element form) and the bundled inclusion\n    32\t  natural transformation `pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C`.\n    33\t-/\n    34\t\n    35\tset_option autoImplicit false\n    36\t\n    37\tuniverse u\n    38\t\n    39\topen CategoryTheory\n    40\t\n    41\tnamespace AlgebraicGeometry\n    42\t\n    43\tvariable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}\n    44\t  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]\n    45\t\n    46\tnoncomputable section\n    47\t\n    48\t/-! ## The degree at a field point -/\n    49\t\n    50\t/-- **The degree of an étale Picard class at a field point** (gap G-D6): restrict along\n    51\t`t : overSpec k K ⟶ T`, collapse by the affine comparison to a plus class of the test\n    52\talgebra `K`, and take its degree (SB-6).  Well-defined in the representative of the\n    53\trestricted class by the zigzag (WD) underlying `PicEtAff.degAff`. -/\n    54\tdef degAt {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) {K : Type u} [Field K]\n    55\t    [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : ℤ :=\n    56\t  PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))\n    57\t\n    58\tsection DegAt\n    59\t\n    60\tvariable {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]\n    61\t\n    62\t/-- The trivial class has degree zero at every field point. -/\n    63\t@[simp]\n    64\ttheorem degAt_one (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : degAt (1 : picEt C T) t = 0 := by\n    65\t  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t 1)) = 0\n    66\t  rw [map_one, map_one, PicEtAff.degAff_one]\n    67\t\n    68\t/-- The degree at a field point of a product of classes is the sum of the degrees. -/\n    69\ttheorem degAt_mul (lam mu : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :\n    70\t    degAt (lam * mu) t = degAt lam t + degAt mu t := by\n    71\t  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t (lam * mu)))\n    72\t      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))\n    73\t        + PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t mu))\n    74\t  rw [map_mul, map_mul, PicEtAff.degAff_mul]\n    75\t\n    76\t/-- The degree at a field point of an inverse class is the negation of the degree. -/\n    77\ttheorem degAt_inv (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :\n    78\t    degAt lam⁻¹ t = -degAt lam t := by\n    79\t  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam⁻¹)) = -degAt lam t\n    80\t  rw [map_inv, map_inv, PicEtAff.degAff_inv]\n    81\t  rfl\n    82\t\n    83\t/-- **Functoriality of the degree at field points** (restriction form): the degree of a\n    84\trestricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at the composed\n    85\tfield point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting — this is what makes the stability of the\n    86\tdegree-zero subfunctor definitional. -/\n    87\ttheorem degAt_picEtMap (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :\n    88\t    degAt (picEtMap C f lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) := by\n    89\t  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t' (picEtMap C f lam)))\n    90\t      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C (t' ≫ f) lam))\n    91\t  rw [← picEtMap_comp]\n    92\t\n    93\t/-- Functoriality of the degree at field points, functor form. -/\n    94\ttheorem degAt_picEtFunctor_map (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T)\n    95\t    (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :\n    96\t    degAt ((picEtFunctor C).map f.op lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) :=\n    97\t  degAt_picEtMap f lam t'\n    98\t\n    99\tend DegAt\n   100\t\n   101\t/-! ## The degree-zero subfunctor -/\n   102\t\n   103\tvariable (C) in\n   104\t/-- **The degree-zero subgroup** of the étale Picard group of a test object: the\n   105\tclasses of degree zero at every field point of the test.  The object part of the\n   106\tdegree-zero Picard functor `pic0Functor` (gap G-D7). -/\n   107\tdef pic0Subgroup (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup (picEt C T) where\n   108\t  carrier := {lam | ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),\n   109\t    degAt lam t = 0}\n   110\t  one_mem' := by\n   111\t    intro K _ _ t\n   112\t    exact degAt_one t\n   113\t  mul_mem' := by\n   114\t    intro a b ha hb K _ _ t\n   115\t    rw [degAt_mul, ha K t, hb K t, add_zero]\n   116\t  inv_mem' := by\n   117\t    intro a ha K _ _ t\n   118\t    rw [degAt_inv, ha K t, neg_zero]\n   119\t\n   120\t/-- Membership in the degree-zero subgroup: degree zero at every field point. -/\n   121\ttheorem mem_pic0Subgroup_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} :\n   122\t    lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T\n   123\t      ↔ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),\n   124\t          degAt lam t = 0 :=\n   125\t  Iff.rfl\n   126\t\n   127\tvariable (C) in\n   128\t/-- Restriction of degree-zero classes along a morphism of test objects: the map part\n   129\tof the degree-zero Picard functor.  The stability of the degree-zero condition is\n   130\tdefinitional through the functoriality `degAt_picEtMap` of the degree at field\n   131\tpoints. -/\n   132\tdef pic0Map {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) :\n   133\t    pic0Subgroup C T →* pic0Subgroup C T' :=\n   134\t  ((picEtMap C f).comp (pic0Subgroup C T).subtype).codRestrict (pic0Subgroup C T')\n   135\t    fun lam K _ _ t' => (degAt_picEtMap f (lam : picEt C T) t').trans (lam.2 K (t' ≫ f))\n   136\t\n   137\t/-- The underlying étale Picard class of a restricted degree-zero class — the\n   138\tnaturality square of the subfunctor inclusion, element form. -/\n   139\t@[simp]\n   140\ttheorem pic0Map_coe {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)\n   141\t    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T) :\n   142\t    (pic0Map C f lam : picEt C T') = picEtMap C f (lam : picEt C T) :=\n   143\t  rfl\n   144\t\n   145\tvariable (C) in\n   146\t/-- **The degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup\n   147\tsubfunctor of the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor `picEtFunctor C` of classes\n   148\tof degree zero at every field point of the test object.  This is the binding carrier of\n   149\tthe Wave-4 representability statement (design §2.7): the Jacobian represents *this*\n   150\tfunctor. -/\n   151\tdef pic0Functor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} where\n   152\t  obj T := CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop)\n   153\t  map g := CommGrpCat.ofHom (pic0Map C g.unop)\n   154\t  map_id T := by\n   155\t    ext lam U\n   156\t    exact congrArg (fun z : picEt C T.unop => z.1 U) (picEtMap_id C (lam : picEt C T.unop))\n   157\t  map_comp g h := by\n   158\t    ext lam U\n   159\t    exact congrArg (fun z => z.1 U) (picEtMap_comp C g.unop h.unop (lam : picEt C _))\n   160\t\n   161\t@[simp]\n   162\ttheorem pic0Functor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :\n   163\t    (pic0Functor C).obj T = CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :=\n   164\t  rfl\n   165\t\n   166\t@[simp]\n   167\ttheorem pic0Functor_map {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')\n   168\t    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :\n   169\t    (pic0Functor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=\n   170\t  rfl\n   171\t\n   172\tvariable (C) in\n   173\t/-- The inclusion of the degree-zero subfunctor into the étale-sheafified relative\n   174\tPicard functor, as a natural transformation — the naturality square consumers cite\n   175\t(bundled form of `pic0Map_coe`). -/", "parent_tool_use_id": "toolu_bdrk_01XCYXENFtJdVaZdRSLrp5Rn", "subagent_type": "general-purpose"}, "usage": null}

All rights reserved.\n     3\tReleased under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.\n     4\tAuthors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors\n     5\t-/\n     6\timport Mathlib\n     7\timport AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RelPicFunctor\n     8\t\n     9\t/-!\n    10\t# The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor\n    11\t\n    12\tThis file constructs the **étale-sheafified relative Picard functor**\n    13\t`Pic_{(C/k)ét}` of a smooth proper curve `C/k` and proves that it *is* a sheaf\n    14\tfor the étale topology — the object whose representability is the project's\n    15\tcentral open obligation (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`).\n    16\t\n    17\t## Why the sheafification is the right object\n    18\t\n    19\tThe relative Picard presheaf `T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`\n    20\t(`Scheme.PicSharp.relPresheaf`, Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`) is in general **not\n    21\ta sheaf**, not even for the Zariski topology (Kleiman §2, L1292–L1302): a line\n    22\tbundle on `C ×_k T` can be trivial on each member of a cover of `T` without\n    23\tbeing trivial modulo `π_T^* Pic(T)`, because the gluing data is a `Pic`-class\n    24\tof the overlaps. Kleiman's representability theorem (§4 Thm. `th:main`) is\n    25\ttherefore a statement about the associated **étale** sheaf, and it is that\n    26\tstatement which is true over an arbitrary base field with no rational-point\n    27\thypothesis.\n    28\t\n    29\tThere are two ways to reach a sheaf, and they differ in what has to be\n    30\tsupplied:\n    31\t\n    32\t1. assume `C` has a `k`-rational point. Then Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 says the\n    33\t   comparison `Pic_{C/k} → Pic_{(C/k)ét}` is already bijective, so the plain\n    34\t   presheaf is the sheaf. This is *strictly weaker* than the challenge, whose\n    35\t   curve need not have a rational point, and it is the route the conditional\n    36\t   `Scheme.picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` records;\n    37\t2. sheafify. Nothing is assumed about `C(k)`, and the sheaf axiom holds by\n    38\t   construction. This is the route realised here and the one the project\n    39\t   claims (owner decision of 2026-07-28).\n    40\t\n    41\t## The site\n    42\t\n    43\tMathlib `v4.31` carries the big étale site on schemes,\n    44\t`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleTopology = grothendieckTopology @Etale`\n    45\t(`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean`). The relative Picard presheaf\n    46\tlives on the slice `Over (Spec k)` rather than on `Scheme`, so the topology is\n    47\ttransported along the localisation of SGA 4 III 5.2.1, available in Mathlib as\n    48\t`GrothendieckTopology.over`: a sieve of `T : Over (Spec k)` covers iff the\n    49\tcorresponding sieve of `T.left` covers étale-locally. That transport is where\n    50\t\"the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`\" becomes a definition rather than a parameter,\n    51\tand it is what lets the sheaf property below be a *theorem* rather than a\n    52\thypothesis.\n    53\t\n    54\t## Main definitions\n    55\t\n    56\t* `Scheme.etaleTopologyOver k` — the étale topology on `(Sch/k) = Over (Spec k)`.\n    57\t* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf C` — `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, a bundled\n    58\t  `Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat`, obtained by sheafifying the\n    59\t  relative Picard presheaf.\n    60\t* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf_isSheaf` — the sheaf property, extracted as a\n    61\t    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :\n    62\t    Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1} :=\n    63\t  (CategoryTheory.presheafToSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}).obj\n    64\t    (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)\n    65\t\n    66\t/-- **The sheaf property of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, as a standalone statement.**\n    67\t\n    68\tThe underlying presheaf of `PicSharp.etaleSheaf C` satisfies the sheaf axiom\n    69\tfor the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`. This is `Sheaf.cond` of the bundled\n    70\tobject, stated separately because it is the property consumers cite: a\n    71\trepresenting scheme for `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` exists only because the functor being\n    72\trepresented is an étale sheaf (a representable functor is a sheaf for any\n    73\tsubcanonical topology, so a non-sheaf can never be representable — which is\n    74\texactly why the unsheafified `relPresheaf` needs a rational point).\n    75\t\n    76\tProved, not assumed: sheafification produces a sheaf. -/\n    77\ttheorem etaleSheaf_isSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))\n    78\t    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :\n    79\t    Presheaf.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (etaleSheaf C).obj :=\n    80\t  (etaleSheaf C).property\n    81\t\n    82\t/-- **The comparison map** `Pic_{C/k} ⟶ Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, i.e. the unit of the\n    83\tsheafification adjunction at the relative Picard presheaf.\n    84\t\n    85\tKleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 (`th:comp`) says this map is an isomorphism when `C` has a\n    86\t`k`-rational point (and `O_S = f_* O_X` universally, automatic here). Over an\n    87\tarbitrary base field it is only a comparison: the honest object is the target,\n    88\twhich is why the representability obligation is stated there. -/\n    89\tnoncomputable def toEtaleSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))\n    90\t    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :\n    91\t    PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ (etaleSheaf C).obj :=\n    92\t  CategoryTheory.toSheafify (etaleTopologyOver k) (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)\n    93\t\n    94\t/-- The universal property of the sheafification, in the form consumers use:\n    95\tevery morphism from the relative Picard presheaf to (the underlying presheaf\n    96\tof) an étale sheaf factors uniquely through `toEtaleSheaf`.\n    97\t\n    98\tThis is what makes `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` the *canonical* choice rather than one\n    99\tsheaf among many, and it is the step that turns a representing scheme for the\n   100\tsheaf into a universal receiver of relative Picard classes. -/\n   101\tnoncomputable def etaleSheafHomEquiv {k : Type u} [Field k]\n   102\t    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))\n   103\t    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]\n   104\t    (G : Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) :\n   105\t    (etaleSheaf C ⟶ G) ≃ (PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ G.obj) :=\n   106\t  ((CategoryTheory.sheafificationAdjunction (etaleTopologyOver k)\n   107\t    AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).homEquiv (PicSharp.relPresheaf C) G)\n   108\t\n   109\tend PicSharp\n   110\t\n   111\tnamespace PicScheme\n   112\t\n   113\t/-! ## §3. The set-valued functor that gets represented -/\n   114\t\n   115\t/-- **The functor whose representability is the project's central obligation**:\n   116\tthe étale-sheafified relative Picard functor with its group structure\n   117\tforgotten,\n   118\t\n   119\t```\n   120\tpicEt C : (Sch/k)^op ⥤ Type (u+1),   T ↦ Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T).\n   121\t```\n   122\t\n   123\tRepresentability is a statement about the underlying set-valued functor; the\n   124\tgroup structure is transported back onto the representing scheme by Yoneda\n   125\t(`PicScheme.groupSchemeStructure`), exactly as for the unsheafified\n   126\t`picSharp`.\n   127\t\n   128\tContrast with `picSharp C = relPresheaf C ⋙ forget`: that functor is\n   129\trepresentable only under a rational-point hypothesis (it is not even a\n   130\tZariski sheaf otherwise), whereas *this* one is the object of Kleiman §4\n   131\tThm. `th:main` and its representability needs no hypothesis on `C(k)`. -/\n   132\tnoncomputable def picEt {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))\n   133\t    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :\n   134\t    (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u+1) :=\n   135\t  (PicSharp.etaleSheaf C).obj ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}\n   136\t\n   137\t/-- The comparison `picSharp C ⟶ picEt C` of set-valued functors, the\n   138\tset-level shadow of `PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf`. An isomorphism under a\n   139\t`k`-rational point (Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5), a comparison in general.\n   140\t\n   141\tThe source is written out as `PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget _` rather than as\n   142\t`picSharp C`, which is the *same functor by definition* but is declared in the\n   143\tdownstream `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean` (that file imports this one, so\n   144\tthe name is not available here). -/\n   145\tnoncomputable def picEtComparison {k : Type u} [Field k]\n   146\t    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))\n   147\t    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :\n   148\t    PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1} ⟶ picEt C :=\n   149\t  CategoryTheory.Functor.whiskerRight (PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf C)\n   150\t    (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1})\n   151\t\n   152\t/-- **`picEt` is an étale sheaf of sets.**\n   153\t\n   154\tThe sheaf property of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` survives forgetting the group structure,\n   155\tbecause the forgetful functor `AddCommGrpCat ⥤ Type` preserves the limits the\n   156\tsheaf condition is stated by. Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting, which is what makes the\n    23\t  degree-zero subfunctor stability definitional.\n    24\t* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Subgroup C T` — the subgroup of classes of degree zero at\n    25\t  *every* field point of `T` (membership: `mem_pic0Subgroup_iff`).\n    26\t* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Functor C : (Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat` — **the\n    27\t  degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup\n    28\t  subfunctor of `picEtFunctor C` cut out by the degree-zero condition, the binding\n    29\t  carrier of the Wave-4 representability statement (`RepresentableBy`, design §2.7).\n    30\t  The restriction maps are `pic0Map`, with underlying-class equation `pic0Map_coe`\n    31\t  (the naturality square of the inclusion, element form) and the bundled inclusion\n    32\t  natural transformation `pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C`.\n    33\t-/\n    34\t\n    35\tset_option autoImplicit false\n    36\t\n    37\tuniverse u\n    38\t\n    39\topen CategoryTheory\n    40\t\n    41\tnamespace AlgebraicGeometry\n    42\t\n    43\tvariable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}\n    44\t  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]\n    45\t\n    46\tnoncomputable section\n    47\t\n    48\t/-! ## The degree at a field point -/\n    49\t\n    50\t/-- **The degree of an étale Picard class at a field point** (gap G-D6): restrict along\n    51\t`t : overSpec k K ⟶ T`, collapse by the affine comparison to a plus class of the test\n    52\talgebra `K`, and take its degree (SB-6).  Well-defined in the representative of the\n    53\trestricted class by the zigzag (WD) underlying `PicEtAff.degAff`. -/\n    54\tdef degAt {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) {K : Type u} [Field K]\n    55\t    [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : ℤ :=\n    56\t  PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))\n    57\t\n    58\tsection DegAt\n    59\t\n    60\tvariable {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]\n    61\t\n    62\t/-- The trivial class has degree zero at every field point. -/\n    63\t@[simp]\n    64\ttheorem degAt_one (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : degAt (1 : picEt C T) t = 0 := by\n    65\t  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t 1)) = 0\n    66\t  rw [map_one, map_one, PicEtAff.degAff_one]\n    67\t\n    68\t/-- The degree at a field point of a product of classes is the sum of the degrees. -/\n    69\ttheorem degAt_mul (lam mu : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :\n    70\t    degAt (lam * mu) t = degAt lam t + degAt mu t := by\n    71\t  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t (lam * mu)))\n    72\t      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))\n    73\t        + PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t mu))\n    74\t  rw [map_mul, map_mul, PicEtAff.degAff_mul]\n    75\t\n    76\t/-- The degree at a field point of an inverse class is the negation of the degree. -/\n    77\ttheorem degAt_inv (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :\n    78\t    degAt lam⁻¹ t = -degAt lam t := by\n    79\t  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam⁻¹)) = -degAt lam t\n    80\t  rw [map_inv, map_inv, PicEtAff.degAff_inv]\n    81\t  rfl\n    82\t\n    83\t/-- **Functoriality of the degree at field points** (restriction form): the degree of a\n    84\trestricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at the composed\n    85\tfield point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting — this is what makes the stability of the\n    86\tdegree-zero subfunctor definitional. -/\n    87\ttheorem degAt_picEtMap (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :\n    88\t    degAt (picEtMap C f lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) := by\n    89\t  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t' (picEtMap C f lam)))\n    90\t      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C (t' ≫ f) lam))\n    91\t  rw [← picEtMap_comp]\n    92\t\n    93\t/-- Functoriality of the degree at field points, functor form. -/\n    94\ttheorem degAt_picEtFunctor_map (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T)\n    95\t    (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :\n    96\t    degAt ((picEtFunctor C).map f.op lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) :=\n    97\t  degAt_picEtMap f lam t'\n    98\t\n    99\tend DegAt\n   100\t\n   101\t/-! ## The degree-zero subfunctor -/\n   102\t\n   103\tvariable (C) in\n   104\t/-- **The degree-zero subgroup** of the étale Picard group of a test object: the\n   105\tclasses of degree zero at every field point of the test. All rights reserved.\n     3\tReleased under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.\n     4\tAuthors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors\n     5\t-/\n     6\timport AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.JacobianData\n     7\timport AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0SigmaSheaf\n     8\t\n     9\t/-!\n    10\t# Producing the Jacobian representability datum from a Zariski chart family\n    11\t\n    12\tThe pinned datum `JacobianData C` of the curve `C` bundles a representing object for the\n    13\tdegree-zero Picard functor together with the two finiteness certificates of that object.\n    14\tThis file constructs it: first from a bare representation (`JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy`),\n    15\tand then — the substance — from a Zariski chart family of the Σ-extension sheaf, whose glued\n    16\tscheme is the representing object and whose charts carry the finiteness.\n    17\t\n    18\t## Main declarations\n    19\t\n    20\t* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy` — a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor C`\n    21\t  by `J`, plus `LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom` and `QuasiCompact J.hom`, is a `JacobianData C`.\n    22\t* `AlgebraicGeometry.gluedHom` / `AlgebraicGeometry.gluedOfCharts` — the glued scheme of a chart\n    23\t  family, placed over the base field by the Σ-component of the universal element of the\n    24\t  representation it induces.\n    25\t* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartHom` — the structure morphism `X i ⟶ Spec k` of the `i`-th chart:\n    26\t  the Σ-component of the element of `pic0SigmaFunctor C` classified by `f i`.\n    27\t* `AlgebraicGeometry.toGlued_comp_gluedHom` — **the compatibility of the two**: the glue map\n    28\t  `X i ⟶ gluedOfCharts` composed with the structure morphism of the glued object is exactly\n    29\t  `chartHom i`.  So the charts are charts *over the base field*, and the glued object is\n    30\t  covered by them as a `k`-scheme.\n    31\t* `AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom` — being locally of finite type is local\n    32\t  on the source, so it descends from the charts to the glued object.\n    33\t* `AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_gluedHom` — over the affine base `Spec k`, quasi-compactness\n    34\t  of the glued object is compactness of its space, which a finite family of compact charts\n    35\t  supplies.\n    36\t* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofCharts` — **the first producer of the Jacobian datum**:\n    37\t  a finite Zariski chart family of relatively representable open immersions into\n    38\t  `pic0SigmaSheaf C`, jointly locally surjective, with quasi-compact charts that are locally of\n    39\t  finite type over `k`, yields `JacobianData C`.\n    40\t\n    41\t## The hypothesis bundle\n    42\t\n    43\tEvery declaration here carries exactly the three hypotheses of the frozen `Jacobian` of\n    44\t`Challenge.lean` — `IsProper`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1`, `GeometricallyIrreducible`.  The\n    45\t`GeometricallyReduced C.hom` hypothesis of `Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean` is *not* an extra assumption:\n    46\ta morphism smooth of relative dimension `1` is smooth (`Smooth.of_smoothOfRelativeDimension_one`)\n    47\tand a smooth morphism is geometrically reduced (`Smooth.geometricallyReduced`), both global\n    48\tinstances of `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.GeometricallyReduced`, so instance resolution supplies it\n    49\tfrom the frozen bundle.  The `example` at the end of this file is the machine-checked record.\n    50\t-/\n    51\t\n    52\tset_option autoImplicit false\n    53\tset_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3\n    54\t\n    55\tuniverse u\n    56\t\n    57\topen CategoryTheory Limits Opposite\n    58\t\n    59\tnamespace AlgebraicGeometry\n    60\t\n    61\tvariable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))\n    62\tvariable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]\n    63\tvariable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]\n    64\t\n    65\t/-! ## Packaging a representation as the datum -/\n    66\t\n    67\t/-- **Package a representation of the degree-zero Picard functor**, with its two finiteness\n    68\tcertificates, as the pinned Jacobian datum.  The representation is stated in the\n    69\t`pic0TypeFunctor` spelling; that abbreviation unfolds to the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage that\n    70\t`JacobianData.rep` is typed against. -/\n    71\tnoncomputable def JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))\n    72\t    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)\n    73\t    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom) :\n    74\t    JacobianData C where\n    75\t  J := J\n    76\t  rep := rep\n    77\t  locallyOfFiniteType := hlft\n    78\t  quasiCompact := hqc\n    79\t\n    80\t@[simp]\n    81\tlemma JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy_J (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))\n    82\t    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)\n    83\t    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom) :\n    84\t    (JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C J rep hlft hqc).J = J :=\n    85\t  rfl\n    86\t\n    87\t@[simp]\n    88\tlemma JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy_rep (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))\n    89\t    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)\n    90\t    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom) :\n    91\t    (JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C J rep hlft hqc).rep = rep :=\n    92\t  rfl\n    93\t\n    94\t/-- The universal property of a packaged datum is the packaged representation. -/\n    95\t@[simp]\n    96\tlemma JacobianData.homEquiv_ofRepresentableBy (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))\n    97\t    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)\n    98\t    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom)\n    99\t    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (g : T ⟶ J) :\n   100\t    (JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C J rep hlft hqc).homEquiv g = rep.homEquiv g :=\n   101\t  rfl\n   102\t\n   103\t/-! ## The chart family and its glued object -/\n   104\t\n   105\tsection Charts\n   106\t\n   107\tvariable {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}\n   108\t  (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)\n   109\t\n   110\t/-- **The structure morphism of the `i`-th chart** over the base field: the Σ-component of the\n   111\telement of `pic0SigmaFunctor C` classified by `f i`.  A chart of the degree-zero Picard sheaf\n   112\tis by construction a scheme *together with* a map to `Spec k`, namely the base over which the\n   113\tline bundle it classifies lives; this is that map. -/\n   114\tnoncomputable def chartHom (i : ι) : X i ⟶ Spec (.of k) := (yonedaEquiv (f i)).1\n   115\t\n   116\tvariable (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))\n   117\tvariable [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]\n   118\t\n   119\t/-- **The structure morphism of the glued object of a chart family**: mathlib's 01JJ engine\n   120\tglues the charts into a scheme representing the Σ-extension sheaf, and the Σ-component of the\n   121\tuniversal element of that representation is the map of that scheme to `Spec k`. -/\n   122\tnoncomputable abbrev gluedHom :\n   123\t    (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued ⟶ Spec (.of k) :=\n   124\t  ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv\n   125\t    (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1\n   126\t\n   127\t/-- **The glued object of a chart family**, as a scheme over the base field.  This is the\n   128\tobject represented by `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`. -/\n   129\tnoncomputable abbrev gluedOfCharts : Over (Spec (.of k)) := Over.mk (gluedHom C f hf)\n   130\t\n   131\t  exact HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr ‹_›\n   132\t\n   133\t/-! ## The producer -/\n   134\t\n   135\t/-- **The first producer of the Jacobian datum**: a Zariski chart family of relatively\n   136\trepresentable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf of the degree-zero Picard functor,\n   137\tjointly locally surjective, indexed by a finite type, with quasi-compact charts that are locally\n   138\tof finite type over the base field, produces the pinned representability datum of the curve.\n   139\t\n   140\tThe representing object is the glued scheme of the family, placed over `Spec k` by the\n   141\tΣ-component of the universal element; the two certificates are `locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom`\n   142\tand `quasiCompact_gluedHom`. -/\n   143\tnoncomputable def JacobianData.ofCharts [Finite ι]\n   144\t    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))\n   145\t    (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :\n   146\t    JacobianData C :=\n   147\t  JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C (gluedOfCharts C f hf)\n   148\t    (pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C f hf)\n   149\t    (locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom C f hf hlft)\n   150\t    (quasiCompact_gluedHom C f hf hcpt)\n   151\t\n   152\t@[simp]\n   153\tlemma JacobianData.ofCharts_J [Finite ι]\n   154\t    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))\n   155\t    (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :\n   156\t    (JacobianData.ofCharts C f hf hlft hcpt).J = gluedOfCharts C f hf :=\n   157\t  rfl\n   158\t\n   159\t/-- **The producer for an infinite atlas**: same as `JacobianData.ofCharts`, but the index type\n   160\tis arbitrary and quasi-compactness of the glued object is supplied directly instead of being\n   161\tderived from finitely many compact charts.\n   162\t\n   163\tThis is the form the classical construction needs.  The charts of the degree-zero Picard functor\n   164\tare indexed by divisor *classes* — one chart per class whose twisted fibre class has an effective\n   165\twitness — and that index set is not finite; compactness of the glued object is then a genuine\n   166\ttheorem about the Jacobian (it is the union of the images of a *quasi-compact* divisor scheme\n   167\tunder the Abel map), not a consequence of finiteness of the atlas.  Note that the\n   168\tlocally-of-finite-type certificate still descends from the charts with no finiteness hypothesis\n   169\twhatsoever: `locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom` never uses `Finite ι`. -/\n   170\tnoncomputable def JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace\n   171\t    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))\n   172\t    (hcpt : CompactSpace (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued) :\n   173\t    JacobianData C :=\n   174\t  JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C (gluedOfCharts C f hf)\n   175\t    (pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C f hf)\n   176\t    (locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom C f hf hlft)\n   177\t    (HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr hcpt)\n   178\t\n   179\t@[simp]\n   180\tlemma JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace_J\n   181\t    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))\n   182\t    (hcpt : CompactSpace (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued) :\n   183\t    (JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace C f hf hlft hcpt).J = gluedOfCharts C f hf :=\n   184\t  rfl\n   185\t\n   186\tend Charts\n   187\t\n   188\t/-! ## The hypothesis bundle of the frozen `Jacobian` suffices\n   189\t\n   190\t`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean` introduces `[GeometricallyReduced C.hom]` before its sheaf and\n   191\trepresentability statements, while the frozen `Jacobian` of `Challenge.lean` carries only\n   192\t`IsProper`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1` and `GeometricallyIrreducible`.  There is no gap:\n   193\tgeometric reducedness is *derived* from smoothness of relative dimension one by the global\n   194\tinstances of `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.GeometricallyReduced`, which is in the import closure of\n   195\t`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean`.  Hence every declaration above elaborates under the frozen bundle alone,\n   196\tand the example below records it. -/\n   197\t\n   198\texample : GeometricallyReduced C.hom := inferInstance\n   199\t\n   200\t/-! ## What remains\n   201\t\n   202\t`JacobianData.ofCharts` reduces the frozen `Jacobian` of `Challenge.lean` — that is, the\n   203\tproduction of `jacobianData C : JacobianData C`, from which `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J` —\n   204\tto a single geometric statement about the degree-zero Picard sheaf of the curve, namely the\n   205\texistence of a finite Zariski atlas:\n   206\t\n   207\t> there exist a finite index type `ι`, schemes `X : ι → Scheme`, and morphisms of presheaves\n   208\t> `f i : yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaFunctor C` such that\n   209\t>\n   210\t> 1. **(relative representability)** each `f i` is a relatively representable open immersion,\n   211\t>    `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i)`;\n   212\t> 2. **(coverage)** the family is jointly locally surjective for the big Zariski topology,\n   213\t>    `Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)`;\n   214\t> 3. **(chart finiteness)** each chart is locally of finite type over the base field with\n   215\t>    respect to its own structure morphism, `LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i)`, and each\n   216\t>    chart space is quasi-compact, `CompactSpace (X i)`.\n   217\t\n   218\tNothing else about the Picard functor is needed: the sheaf condition is already discharged\n   219\t(`pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf`), the gluing is mathlib's (`Scheme.LocalRepresentability`), the\n   220\tΣ-descent to the slice is already discharged (`Functor.RepresentableBy.overSlice`), and the two\n   221\tcertificates of the glued object are discharged here from (3).\n   222\t\n   223\tConditions (1) and (2) are the geometric input — they are what the divisor-scheme/Abel-map\n   224\tmachinery of the `DivScheme…` and `DivRep…` files exists to produce, one chart being carved out\n   225\tof a symmetric power of the curve by an effectivity locus.  Condition (3) is a property of those\n   226\tcharts alone and does not interact with the Picard functor at all.\n   227\t\n   228\tIf the atlas that machinery produces is *not* finitely indexed — and the classical one is not,\n   229\tits charts being indexed by divisor classes — then `JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace` is the\n   230\tform to use: `ι` is then arbitrary, condition (3) weakens to `LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i)`\n   231\talone, and the second certificate becomes the single statement `CompactSpace` of the glued", "parent_tool_use_id": "toolu_bdrk_01XCYXENFtJdVaZdRSLrp5Rn", "subagent_type": "general-purpose"}, "usage": null}

All rights reserved.\n     3\tReleased under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.\n     4\tAuthors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors\n     5\t-/\n     6\timport AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen\n     7\timport AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0AtlasFromDivRep\n     8\t\n     9\t/-!\n    10\t# C9b: the restricted chart map and the `(f, hf)` pair\n    11\t\n    12\t`Picard/Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean` builds the Abel chart map `abelSigmaChart` out of a\n    13\trepresentation of the divisor functor, and its header states — correctly — that\n    14\t`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart …)` is **false as stated for the whole divisor\n    15\tscheme**: the Abel map has projective spaces `|D|` as fibres, so it is not even a\n    16\tmonomorphism.  It becomes an open immersion only after restriction to the locus where the\n    17\tfibre is a single point.\n    18\t\n    19\tThis file supplies the restriction, which is the half of C9b that needs no new mathematics\n    20\tonce `chartLocus` exists — and it makes precise which half does.\n    21\t\n    22\t## What C9b consists of, and which part is here\n    23\t\n    24\t`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) consumes a pair\n    25\t`(f, hf)`.  Producing it from `abelSigmaChart` factors into exactly two steps:\n    26\t\n    27\t1. **restrict the source along an open immersion** — `restrictChart` below.  Given any open\n    28\t   `V ⊆ D.left`, precomposing `abelSigmaChart` with `yoneda.map V.ι` gives a chart map out of\n    29\t   `V`, and this is a *composition* of presheaf morphisms.  Landed here, sorry-free.\n    30\t2. **certify the restricted map an open immersion of presheaves** — the honest content.\n    31\t   `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` (mathlib `MorphismProperty.relative`) has two clauses:\n    32\t   relative representability, and the open-immersion property of every represented pullback.\n    33\t   Step 1 supplies the *left* factor of both clauses for free\n    34\t   (`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map_of_isOpenImmersion` +\n    35\t   `MorphismProperty.relative_isStableUnderComposition`), so what remains is exactly the\n    36\t   corresponding statement for `abelSigmaChart` restricted to `V = chartLocus`, i.e.\n    37\t   CHART-U(c): on the chart locus the Abel map is a bijection onto its image because the\n    38\t   normalized effective representative is unique there (DAT-C GAP-2).\n    39\t\n    40\tSo: the *composition* half of the `hf` certificate is discharged here, unconditionally; the\n    41\t*chart-locus* half is CHART-U(c) and is stated but not proved (it needs GAP-2 plus the\n    42\tclassifier, and the openness of the locus itself, `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`).\n    43\t\n    44\t## CORRECTION 2026-07-29: step 2 above is itself TWO clauses, not one\n    45\t\n    46\tThe description of step 2 as \"*the* honest content\" is right that it is not bookkeeping and\n    47\twrong that it is a single obligation.  `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` conjoins **relative\n    48\trepresentability** (the fibre product is a scheme at all) with **the property clause** (each\n    49\trepresented pullback is an open immersion).  The GAP-2/classifier story is the input to the\n    50\tsecond only.  The first needs just an open of the test, and `chartLocus` is one\n    51\tunconditionally — so it is not CERT-Σ-gated at all.\n    52\t\n    53\tThat split is landed: `Picard/Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean` (the criterion, from\n    54\telementwise data) and `Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean` (instantiated at the Abel chart,\n    55\treducing the datum from four fields to three).  `IsChartUniv` below is unchanged as a\n    56\t*statement* — it is still the right pin — but it is no longer the right unit of *pricing*.\n    57\tRead `isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` for what a lane now actually owes.\n    58\t\n    59\t## Main declarations\n    60\t\n    61\t* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map` — an open immersion of schemes is\n    62\t  an open immersion of presheaves under yoneda.  This is mathlib's `relative_map` at\n    63\t  `P := IsOpenImmersion`, recorded once with the instances it needs discharged.\n    64\t* `AlgebraicGeometry.restrictChart` — the chart map restricted to an open of the source.\n    65\t* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart` — **the composition half of\n    66\t  `hf`**: if the unrestricted chart map is an open immersion of presheaves, so is any\n    67\t  restriction of it along an open immersion.  Unconditional in the restriction.\n    68\t* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartHom_restrictChart` — the structure morphism of a restricted chart\n    69\t  is the restriction of the structure morphism, so the `LocallyOfFiniteType` hypothesis of\n    70\t  `JacobianData.ofCharts` is inherited (being locally of finite type is local on the\n    71\t  source).\n    72\t-/\n    73\t\n    74\tset_option autoImplicit false\n    75\tset_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3\n    76\t\n    77\tuniverse u\n    78\t\n    79\topen CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory\n    80\t\n    81\tnamespace AlgebraicGeometry\n    82\t\n    83\tvariable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}\n    84\tvariable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] {n : ℕ}\n    85\tvariable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]\n    86\tvariable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]\n    87\t\n    88\tnoncomputable section\n    89\t\n    90\t/-! ## An open immersion of schemes is one of presheaves -/\n    91\t\n    92\t/-- **Open immersions transfer through yoneda**: for an open immersion of schemes\n    93\t`g : X ⟶ Y`, the induced map of yoneda presheaves satisfies `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`.\n    94\t\n    95\tThis is mathlib's `MorphismProperty.relative_map` specialised to `F := yoneda` and\n    96\t`P := @IsOpenImmersion`; the two side conditions it needs — that open immersions are stable\n    97\tunder base change, and that yoneda preserves the relevant pullbacks (it is fully faithful and\n    98\t`Scheme` has pullbacks) — are discharged by instances.\n    99\t\n   100\tRecorded as a named lemma because it is the *only* source of `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`\n   101\tfacts anywhere in this tree that does not go through a chart certificate: every restriction\n   102\tof a chart map is built from it. -/\n   103\ttheorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Y)\n   104\t    [IsOpenImmersion g] :\n   105\t    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (yoneda.map g) :=\n   106\t  MorphismProperty.relative_map (P := @IsOpenImmersion) (F := yoneda) ‹IsOpenImmersion g›\n   107\t\n   108\t/-! ## The restricted chart map -/\n   109\t\n   110\t/-- **The chart map restricted to an open of its source.**\n   111\t\n   112\t`f` is the unrestricted chart map (in practice `abelSigmaChart`, whose source is the divisor\n   113\tscheme) and `V` an open subscheme of the source; the restriction is the composition with the\n   114\tyoneda image of the open inclusion.\n   115\t\n   116\tThe point of restricting is that the unrestricted Abel map is *not* an open immersion of\n   117\tpresheaves — see the `Pic0AtlasFromDivRep` header — while its restriction to the locus where\n   118\tthe fibre is a single point is.
